what_happened: An open_thread record (thread_20260421_220352_780dbac8, domain temple-wars,next-move) had 849 chars of question text containing literal </question>, <parameter name="context">, and a prose context payload that was meant to live in the context field. The context field on the record was empty (0 chars). A previous record_open_thread tool call emitted XML-style tool-call scaffolding (the model wrote the call as <question>...</question><parameter name="context">...</parameter> instead of providing question and context as separate JSON arguments). The bridge accepted the call and persisted the entire blob into question. Cleanup: split at marker, moved trailing payload into context, wrote back. Backup at jsonl.bak.20260502. Thread_id rotated 780dbac8 -> eee20bc5 because id is content-derived; old id remains in append-only attention logs (nape, reflexive priors), which is correct historical record.
what_learned: Tool-call scaffolding can leak into stored records when the calling model emits XML-format invocations into a JSON tool boundary. The bridge does not currently validate that string arguments don't contain unescaped tool-call delimiters. Mitigations to consider: (a) validate at write time that question/context/content fields don't contain </question>, <parameter name=, </parameter>, or <system-reminder> tokens; (b) reject or sanitize on detection rather than silently persisting; (c) at minimum, log a warning when these tokens land in user-payload fields. Until then, the chronicle can carry latent contamination that only surfaces when a downstream renderer happens to display the field. Audit pattern: grep open_threads, insights, and learnings for these tokens periodically.
applies_to: record_open_thread, record_insight, record_learning, handoff, close_session — any chronicle write that takes free-text string arguments through the bridge
